intended_object: The predicate that an R-algebra A is smooth at a prime p of A (Stacks 00TB). Here it is taken to mean that the localization A_p is formally smooth over R, as the docstring states.
explanation: The body is exactly `FormallySmooth R (Localization.AtPrime p)`, which is what the docstring says. Stacks 00TB defines smoothness at q as the existence of some g ∉ q with S_g smooth over R. For finitely presented algebras the docstring points to `basicOpen_subset_smoothLocus_iff_smooth` and `isOpen_smoothLocus`, which give that equivalence. For algebras that are not finitely presented the two notions can differ: in a polynomial ring in infinitely many variables, every localization A_p is formally smooth, but no A_g is finitely presented. This is a deliberate choice that the docstring states openly, and the formal-smoothness version is the standard pointwise notion used in this setting. It is stated for arbitrary commutative rings R and A, which is the natural generality. Mathlib has no separate declaration of the same notion: this file is part of Mathlib, and `smoothLocus` is built on top of this definition.
